findings.title: Three I/O paths have no stated bound, and one claim contradicts D7
findings.description:
The failure-mode table is thorough for `thread.run`, but hang handling is missing or inconsistent elsewhere:
- **Logout:** `sq auth logout` starts the runtime and calls `AsyncCodex.logout()`, a new I/O path. No D7 key covers it (`codex.account_timeout_s` is scoped at line 109 to status and post-login confirmation) and no table row gives its hang or error behaviour.
- **Turn startup:** line 82 says the startup hang "is already bounded by `codex.turn_timeout_s`". Lines 107 and 125 scope that timeout to "one `thread.run`", which leaves `AsyncCodex.__aenter__`/`initialize` and `thread_start` outside it.
- **Login startup:** `codex.login_timeout_s` bounds `handle.wait()` only (line 108). Runtime start plus the `login_chatgpt()` / `login_chatgpt_device_code()` call that produces the handle is unbounded.

Fix: state which timeout wraps each of these (widening the existing scopes is enough, no new keys) and add the logout row.

findings.title: `sq auth status` behaviour is undefined when the extra is absent but `~/.codex/auth.json` exists
findings.description:
Status calls `account()` whenever the strategy is `InteractiveLogin` and valid. `OAuthFileStrategy` always implements the Protocol, and validity is file presence. A default-install user who has used the Codex CLI therefore reaches `account_summary()` with `openai_codex` not importable.

The design does not say what happens. The nearest row (line 126) covers "timeout or SDK error" with a WARNING, which would fire on every `sq auth status` for a user who never asked for Codex.

This leaves two stated requirements unmet: "Users who do not want Codex install nothing extra" (line 26) and clean operation without the extra. The Integration Requirements (line 205) name only `sq doctor` and `sq model list`, and the test list (line 199) has no status-without-extra case.

Fix: define the outcome (for example, skip account details and show the `missing_extra_hint()` text with no WARNING) and add the test.

findings.title: Login timeout has no clear owner, and `--timeout` duplicates the config key
findings.description:
`InteractiveLogin.login` takes a required `timeout: float`, while the default lives in the Codex-specific key `codex.login_timeout_s` (line 108). The design never says who reads the key:
- **If the generic CLI reads it** to fill the argument, `cli/commands/auth.py` gains Codex-specific knowledge, the coupling D3 exists to prevent.
- **If the strategy reads it**, the Protocol parameter cannot be a required float.

`account_summary()` and `logout()` take no timeout, so the strategy already owns its other bounds. Fix: make the strategy own the default, with the parameter as `float | None` or removed.

Scope to cut: `sq auth login --timeout` (lines 108, 149). The plan entry does not ask for it, and the config key already makes the value adjustable.

findings.title: Usage handling diverges from the slice 931 contract it consumes
findings.description:
- **Absent usage is logged at DEBUG.** Line 134 contradicts the table's own header (line 118: every row is WARNING or above with a test). It also departs from 931, where "backend reported no token usage" is one WARNING per `handle_message` and no count goes missing "without saying so".
- **Failure-path telemetry is unaddressed.** 931 states that any `ProviderError` leaving `handle_message` carries a `RunTelemetry` snapshot in `telemetry`, which the provider-failure artifact reads. D8 and the failed, interrupted, timeout and transport-closed rows raise `ProviderError` without saying whether `TurnResult.usage` or the turn count is attached. A failed Codex turn would then render usage as not reported even when the SDK supplied it.
- **`turns` is unspecified.** Line 55 says the agent stamps `metadata["turns"]`, but D6 never says what value a Codex `handle_message` records.

Fix: align the absent-usage row with 931 (or remove it from the WARNING-header table and justify it), and state the `telemetry` and `turns` behaviour.

findings.title: Line 76 says `get_provider` raises the install hint; D9 needs it to return the provider
findings.description: "`get_provider("openai-oauth")` can raise the install hint" conflicts with lines 80, 122 and 184, where the raise happens at `create_agent`. It also conflicts with D9, where `sq model list` and `sq doctor` must obtain the provider instance to call `missing_extra_hint()`. Reword so an implementer does not put the raise in the registry lookup.

findings.title: Version upper bound is stated two ways and left as a Project Manager wait
findings.description: D1 (line 97) writes `>=0.159.3,<1`; Special Considerations says the cap "is not decided here". A design step waiting on Project Manager confirmation is not valid under the project rules, so state one value. D1's bound, combined with the real-types drift test at line 200, is a sufficient decision.

findings.title: `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback work is outside the plan entry and its ordering is unclear
findings.description:
The silent-fallback argument justifies handling it in this slice. Three loose ends remain:
- **Ordering:** step 0 runs "before porting anything", but the check is only meaningful against the `openai_codex` runtime that ships. Say which runtime it uses.
- **Lighter option:** line 42 already sends API-key users to the `openai` profile. Removing the fallback outright meets that position with no experiment and no two-branch task, at the cost of dropping an env-key path that may currently work for some users.
- **Kept-fallback case:** `account_summary()` is described only for a `ChatgptAccount` root (line 54). Its result for a key-only account is undefined.

findings.title: Interactive login re-binds the generically named `OAuthFileStrategy` to Codex
findings.description: Slice 128 renamed the strategy because "auth type describes mechanism, not product". Implementing `InteractiveLogin` on it via `login_chatgpt` and `codex.*` keys means any future profile with `auth_type = "oauth"` inherits a ChatGPT login. This is acceptable while Codex is the only user and the class lives under `providers/codex/`. Add the caveat to lines 88-89 next to the existing note about a second adopter.

findings.title: `sq model list` now loads every alias's provider
findings.description: D9 resolves each alias through `ensure_provider_loaded` + `get_provider`, turning a data listing into one that imports every referenced provider package. The design does not say what the row shows if a profile's provider fails to load. One sentence would do (for example, render the row without a marker and log a WARNING) so one bad user profile cannot break the listing.
